correctness.rationale: All three bipolar axioms are proved for products: O1 from product facets, O2 from factor intersections of meeting north/south faces, and O3 from atoms of the product vertex lattice and orthogonal coordinate directions. Projection onto a face, relative interior, normal cone and the convex hull of Cartesian products all factor. Theorem 6.6 in the primary source yields the dimension <=3 base case. The exact rational checker executes on two explicit triangles, verifies all 144 sphere incidences in their nine 4D product cells, and confirms a nonrectangular cutout. It supports but does not replace the general proof.

The additional product-closure lemma supplies precisely that missing step for a large decomposable family.

originality.rationale: The November 10, 2026 primary theorem establishes the orthogonal-cutout implication only in dimensions at most three and proposes it as Conjecture 6.8 for higher dimensions. Its companion proves combinatorial interval-lattice and simplex-subdivision facts but no product closure for the three metric bipolar axioms. The present proof separately verifies all three axioms and exact factorization, extending the conjecture to arbitrary Euclidean products of low-dimensional factors. A previous right-simplex cutout family does not cover products of arbitrary triangles and three-polytopes. Actual published-finding corpus and public searches identified no implication-equivalent prior result. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier result may describe Cartesian product closure under a different name.
The high-dimensional corollary is restricted to decomposable orthogonal products and does not settle the indecomposable case.
The proof uses the published low-dimensional base theorem; its validity was checked at the statement level, not independently reproved in full.

value.rationale: This establishes stability of a nontrivial metric-and-combinatorial class under an operation that raises dimension. It proves a natural, arbitrarily high-dimensional family of an explicit 2026 cutout conjecture for products of arbitrary low-dimensional factors, with an exact geometric and combinatorial description of every cell. It goes beyond single numerical computations and right-simplex examples; its use is constructive face-to-face polyhedral tilings.
